sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Nand Kishor Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

By moving this application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the prayer is made to quash the summoning order dated 17.08.2023 as well as the entire proceedings of Sessions Case (Complaint)
No.1014 of 2022, Mohd. Rahish Khan Vs. Imran Khan and others, under Sections 452, 504, 427,
394, 323, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Sikandara, District Kanpur Dehat, pending in the court of learned 3rd Addl. District and Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (Dacoity Affected Area), Kanpur Dehat.

sentences.text: It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that the applicant no.3 is the daughter-in-law of the opposite party no.2.

When she lodged an FIR on 13.04.2022 against her in-laws including the opposite party no.2, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 354B IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act only in counterblast of this FIR, the present complaint dated 08.06.2022 showing Imran Khan And 5 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145526061/
1 incident dated 16.03.2022 has been filed by the opposite party no.2, which is a false complaint, no such incident took place, hence, the prayer is made accordingly.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A., however, opposed the prayer.

From the perusal of the record, it is found that the FIR of the applicant no.3 was lodged prior to the complaint filed by the opposite party no.2 but at the time of passing the impugned order certainly the applicants were not there to bring in the knowledge of the trial court the FIR lodged by the applicant no.3.

In support of complaint dated 08.06.2022 the statement of complainant/opposite party no.2 under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. and the statements of witnesses Alamvir Khan and Farukh Khan as PW-1 and PW-2 respectively were recorded by the trial court under Section 202 of Cr.P.C.
and on the basis of these oral statements the trial court passed the impugned order.

Nothing has been pointed out before this Court that there is any contradiction in the statements of the complainant or the statements of the witnesses or there is any contradiction in the version of the complaint and the statements of the complainant and his witnesses.
This Court is not under obligation to enquire into the factual dispute of the parties.

As at the time of passing impugned order, the trial court had the statements of the complainant and his witnesses under Sections 200 and 202 of Cr.P.C. respectively supporting the version of the complaint, hence, the trial court was right enough to pass the impugned order on the basis of the evidence produced before it.
No weight is found in the arguments of the applicants' counsel.
The application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. having no merit is hereby rejected.
